transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees (as recorded): Alex Chen, Priya Nair, Samir Gupta (Redwood); Marcos Rivas, Anita Bose, Jon Park, Leah Kim (HelioHealth)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync to review throughput results after last retune. Discussed continuous batching tweaks, concurrency caps, queue backpressure, and burst/bandwidth shaping. Agreed next steps: updated batching config, 4-hour peak sim, pricing note on burst capacity, and scheduling a latency-tail run.

Topics: continuous batching adjustments; concurrency target setting; queue-depth shaping; KV cache TTLs; fallback model and burst pricing; telemetry/traces for 99th+ percentiles.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Okay we're live. Thanks everybody for joining, um, appreciate the time. Today we're doing the Load Sculpting pilot weekly review, I think Priya's got the tuning summary.
[00:14] Priya Nair: Yep, hi all. Quick context — since last week we applied the continuous-batcher change: reduced batch timeout from 25ms to 10ms for short requests, increased max-batch-size to 48 for long tokens, and added a soft concurrency cap per worker. Early results look... mixed.
[00:30] Marcos Rivas: Mixed how? We're trying to hit 900 rps steady with 1.2k burst headroom — last run spiked latency a bit.
[00:38] Priya Nair: Right, so average throughput improved by ~12% but tail latency at p99.9 moved up for sessions longer than 350 tokens. We suspect KV cache TTL misalignment — the cache is getting cold on a subset of model shards during bursts.
[00:55] Anita Bose: Can you explain 'soft concurrency cap' — is that per-GPU or per-inference-worker?
[01:02] Priya Nair: Per-worker, it's applied at the runtime scheduler level. It prevents a single worker from accepting more than N inflight streams; it still allows dynamic batching but stops the worker from starve/locking. We tuned N down to 6 for this run.
[01:12] Jon Park: We saw queue pile-ups at the ingress layer though. The customer's load-generator reported queue-length spikes around minute 23 for the 30m burst test.
[01:20] Priya Nair: Yes, that's the queueing shape issue — continuous batching reduced mean latency but the ingress queueing (we use a 2-tier queue: frontdoor and worker-queue) wasn't smoothing bursts. So we need to add shaping at frontdoor and some headroom for KV warmups.
[01:31] Alex Chen: Quick interjection — Marcos, what's your SLO target again for user-facing calls?
[01:35] Marcos Rivas: We want p95 < 220ms and p99 < 450ms for 95% of traffic, and p99.9 ideally below 900ms except during uncontrollable spikes.
[01:45] Priya Nair: Got it. Current config gets p95 to ~180ms, p99 ~420ms, but p99.9 is around 1.1s in the burst windows we ran.
[01:55] Leah Kim: Which means it's failing the p99.9 target during bursts. Is the fallback model kicking?
[02:00] Priya Nair: Not reliably — fallback to the smaller model was set up but our routing policy deferred to fallback only when queue depth exceeded 120. During the observed burst the queue never exceeded that because requests were building across multiple workers, not a single queue. So fallback didn't fire.
[02:12] Samir Gupta: That's a common gotcha — we can change the policy to consider cluster-wide inflight as a signal, not just per-queue.
[02:18] Marcos Rivas: That would help. Also pricing concern — burst capacity costs climb if fallback isn't used. We need the economics for both fallback and on-demand burst.
[02:26] Alex Chen: I'll send the cost scenarios after this call.
[02:30] [02:31] — 4 minute jump, automated note: screen share started?
[02:35] Priya Nair: Ok, I pushed a small telemetry patch to capture per-shard cache hit rates. Quick numbers: during the 30m burst, shard A hit rate dropped to 48% vs baseline 92%. Shard B stayed high. So it's uneven.
[02:50] Anita Bose: That explains the tail — some requests hit cold shards and pay the KV prefetch penalty. Can we coordinate shard placement so hot prefixes land on fewer shards?
[02:59] Priya Nair: We discussed mapping hot prefixes to hot shards, but that requires a small routing change in your frontdoor layer. We can provide a mapping suggestion.
[03:08] Marcos Rivas: We'll need a short change window. Jon, is that viable in staging this week?
[03:12] Jon Park: Yes we can test mapping in staging on Thursday. Need the mapping by Wednesday EOD.
[03:16] Alex Chen: Action item: Priya provides mapping + updated batch config by 2026-08-02.
[03:22] [03:24] Speaker 2 (possibly Priya): Also we saw a correlation between network egress spikes and latency — some instances in the cluster are doing double-router hops due to a misconfiguration; we'll surface that in the debug traces.
[03:36] Jon Park: I'll look at the egress shaping; staging has stricter NAT rules but prod might still have a path issue.
[03:42] Marcos Rivas: On concurrency targets — we set soft cap 6, what's the plan for raising it?
[03:47] Priya Nair: For next run we'll step to 8 on workers pinned to the high-memory GPU and leave 6 on smaller ones. That gave us a good compromise in internal testing: throughput up ~7% without blowing up p99.9.
[03:59] Leah Kim: Any changes to max_batch_size?
[04:02] Priya Nair: Keep 48 for long tokens, but for short path we suggested micro-batches: max 12 with a 6ms timeout. That keeps latency predictable.
[04:12] Alex Chen: We need to capture cost delta — Samir, can you run the unit economics with those settings?
[04:17] Samir Gupta: Yes, will run cost/per-token delta and include burst pricing assumptions. Expect a note by Tuesday.
[04:22] [04:30] Marcos Rivas: Can we talk about the queueing thresholds? Frontdoor currently drops beyond 2000 queued requests which is too high. We need graceful degradation earlier.
[04:38] Priya Nair: Suggest frontdoor shaping to hold at 1.1k and apply a token-level reject policy with 429+Retry-After to clients that are not latency-sensitive. For interactive flows, we route to low-latency pool.
[04:51] Anita Bose: How do we classify interactive vs async? We have mixed traffic on the same endpoints.
[04:56] Alex Chen: Add a header based on call-type from your app (fast/async). If not present, default to conservative routing.
[05:03] Leah Kim: That's a code change for us, but doable. We'll aim for a toggled rollout.
[05:08] [05:20] Priya Nair: Telemetry ask: we need 99th and 99.9th percentile traces with the request path and shard id. Current traces are aggregated by worker only.
[05:29] Jon Park: We'll add shard id to trace context. Might need a quick patch in your SDK to propagate.
[05:35] Alex Chen: We'll share the SDK snippet.
[05:37] [06:00] — pause — quick informal chat — small cross talk —
[06:10] Marcos Rivas: One observation: when we enabled KV prefetch (aggressive TTL warming) we improved p99.9 for short sessions but cost shots up because of prefetching cold keys at scale. Need a measured TTL per prefix.
[06:23] Priya Nair: Proposal: adaptive TTLs — start short for hot prefixes, lengthen for stable ones. We'll provide a prototype config that sets TTL per prefix weight.
[06:33] Anita Bose: That sounds good, need clarity on memory footprint.
[06:36] Priya Nair: We'll include an estimated memory vs hit-rate curve.
[06:41] Alex Chen: Okay let's recap technical items and owners.
[06:45] Marcos Rivas: Also wanted to flag: our security team asked about audit logs for fallback decisions and routing changes.
[06:51] Alex Chen: Redwood provides audit events; Priya, can we add fallback triggers to the audit stream?
[06:55] Priya Nair: Yes, it's a config flip — we'll include event IDs for fallback, rate-limit engages, and KV-cache-evictions.
[06:62] [06:62 — timestamp slight drift in transcript generator]
[07:10] Leah Kim: Quick question on rollout plan — do we want to do canary by region or by worker type?
[07:15] Priya Nair: Canary by worker type first (high-mem then standard), then region; that isolates instance-profile variables.
[07:22] Marcos Rivas: Sounds safe.
[07:25] [07:45] Priya Nair: I'll enumerate the config changes: 1) continuous-batcher timeouts: short 6ms, long 10ms; 2) per-worker soft caps 6 -> 8 for high-mem; 3) max_batch_size: short 12, long 48; 4) frontdoor queue hold at 1100 with early reject policy; 5) adaptive KV TTL proposal; 6) cluster-wide fallback trigger based on inflight percentiles.
[08:08] Jon Park: We'll test the mapping and add shard id into traces.
[08:12] Alex Chen: Samir will provide cost delta. I'll send burst pricing. Priya will deliver configs and mapping.
[08:20] Leah Kim: Any blockers before next week?
[08:23] Marcos Rivas: Only the staging test scheduling — once we have the mapping we can run the 4h sim.
[08:28] Priya Nair: We'll push configs to the repo and ping you.
[08:31] [08:45] Quick cross-talk and laughter about coffee
[09:00] Alex Chen: Alright last item — telemetry. Marcos can you share a small anonymized trace of the p99.9 event?
[09:07] Marcos Rivas: I'll upload it to the shared folder by end of day.
[09:11] Anita Bose: We'll try to make the header change and the frontdoor toggle in staging on Thursday.
[09:17] Alex Chen: Great. Anything else?
[09:19] [09:22] Priya Nair: One more note — if cluster-wide inflight crosses 75% we'll recommend a fast-fail to async endpoints to preserve interactive SLOs.
[09:29] Jon Park: Implementable.
[09:31] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene same time next week — aim to have the 4h sim results and the cost note.
[09:39] Meeting end.
